editorial.headline: Industrial Management Advice, Nationally Open but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Industrial management consulting is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks its registration on the island.
editorial.body:
Nationally, this is an open activity for foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In Bali, however, the immediate answer is different: a foreign investor cannot register it as a PMA activity today. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island on a permanent basis, and this activity falls into that blocked class. The restriction is not a judgement on the value of management advice; it is the practical registration position created by Bali’s risk-based rule.

The underlying work is industrial management and business consulting. It covers advising, guiding, and supporting operations where an industrial enterprise faces organisational or management issues. The scope reaches industrial-service consulting on strategy and organisation; financial decisions; marketing aims and policies; human-resources planning, practices, and policies; and the planning, scheduling, and control of production. In plain terms, the activity is about helping industrial businesses decide how the company should be structured, directed, staffed, marketed, financed, and run.

It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the Bali outcome turns on the risk reading at scale Besar: OSS identifies Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope. Under Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium, that assessment closes the PMA-registration route in the province. It does not erase the national classification; it means that an activity nationally open to up to 100% foreign ownership is nevertheless blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

For an industrial consultant, the clean distinction is geographical and regulatory, not conceptual. The national position says the activity is TERBUKA, with full foreign ownership permitted within the stated ceiling. Bali’s position says that the same activity is blocked for PMA registration because of its risk class, under the moratorium recorded in the Governor’s letter. Any plan centred on Bali has to begin with that present registration reality, rather than treating the national opening as a local clearance.
